samples.text:
The graph shows the percentage of men and women who smoked cigarettes in one country between 1975 and 2020.

In 1975, 52% of men was smoking, which was much higher than women with 28%. After that the percentage of men decreased every five years. It was 41% in 1985, 30% in 2000 and 22% in 2010. In 2020 it was only 15%.

The percentage of women was different at the beginning. It increased from 28% in 1975 to 31% in 1980 and 33% in 1985, which was the highest. After 1985 it started to decrease, and it was 27% in 2000 and 19% in 2010. At the end, in 2020, 12% of women smoked.

The difference between men and women became smaller and smaller. In 1975 the difference was 24%, but in 2020 it was only 3%.

Overall, smoking was decreased for both men and women during the period, and men smoked more than women in all the years. However, women's smoking went up in first ten years before it fell.
samples.why: Overview at the end but accurate · key features, including women's early rise, covered · repetitive phrasing · agreement, passive and article errors, and 'percent' used for points, without blocking meaning.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates the proportion of adult men and women who were smokers in a particular country over a 45-year period from 1975 to 2020.

Overall, smoking rates fell significantly for both sexes, although the pattern for women was slightly different at first. Men were more likely to smoke than women throughout the period, but the gap between them narrowed considerably.

In 1975, over half of men (52%) smoked, compared with 28% of women. The male rate then declined steadily and continuously, falling to 36% in 1990 and 22% in 2010, before reaching just 15% in 2020.

Female smoking, by contrast, initially increased, rising to a peak of 33% in 1985. At this point the difference between men and women was only 8 percentage points. From then on, the rate for women also started to fall, although more slowly than for men in the 1990s, dropping to 27% in 2000 and 12% by 2020. Consequently, by the end of the period the difference between the two sexes had shrank to only three percentage points, compared to 24 points in 1975.
samples.why: Clear overview of shared decline and narrowing gap · key features well highlighted · logical progression · accurate derived comparisons · good range of structures with one verb form slip.

samples.text:
The graph tracks the percentage of adult men and women who smoked cigarettes in one country at five-year intervals between 1975 and 2020.

Overall, smoking became much less common among both men and women over the period. Although men smoked at a higher rate throughout, the gender gap narrowed dramatically, largely because the male rate fell continuously while the female rate initially rose.

In 1975, more than half of adult men smoked (52%), almost double the proportion of women (28%). Male smoking then declined without interruption, at a fairly steady pace, so that by 2000 it had fallen to 30%, and by 2020 it stood at just 15%, less than a third of its original level.

The trend among women was less straightforward. Their smoking rate climbed during the first decade, peaking at 33% in 1985, when it was just 8 points below the male figure. It then entered a gradual decline, falling only modestly to 27% by 2000, before dropping more rapidly to 12% in 2020. As a result, the difference between the sexes shrank from 24 percentage points at the start of the period to a mere 3 points at the end.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected and explained through the narrowing gap · clear overview · accurate figures and derived comparisons · precise, natural vocabulary · wide range of error-free structures.
